questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following electronic transitions in an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone such as mesityl oxide, the transition that undergoes a hypsochromic (blue) shift upon changing the solvent from hexane to ethanol is
optionsEn: $n \to \pi^*$
$\sigma \to \sigma^*$
$\pi \to \pi^*$
$n \to \sigma^*$ of the alkyl C-H bonds
questions.explanationEn: In polar protic solvents like ethanol, hydrogen bonding stabilizes the non-bonding lone pair ($n$) on the carbonyl oxygen far more strongly in the ground state than in the excited state. This increases the $n \to \pi^*$ energy gap, shifting $\lambda_{\max}$ to a shorter wavelength (hypsochromic or blue shift), whereas $\pi \to \pi^*$ exhibits a bathochromic (red) shift.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the IR spectrum of *o*-hydroxyacetophenone, the carbonyl stretching band appears at a significantly lower wavenumber ($\sim 1640\text{ cm}^{-1}$) than in *p*-hydroxyacetophenone ($\sim 1675\text{ cm}^{-1}$) primarily because of
optionsEn: intramolecular chelated hydrogen bonding forming a six-membered ring
stronger inductive withdrawal by the *ortho*-hydroxyl group
steric inhibition of resonance between the aryl ring and the carbonyl group
Fermi resonance with the aromatic C-H overtone bands
questions.explanationEn: In *o*-hydroxyacetophenone, the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ forms a strong intramolecular six-membered chelate hydrogen bond with the carbonyl oxygen. This chelation stabilizes the dipolar resonance contributor ($\text{C}^+-\text{O}^-$), reducing the $\text{C=O}$ force constant and shifting $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ down to $\sim 1640\text{ cm}^{-1}$ even at high dilution.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: An organic compound shows a first-order AX doublet-of-doublets pattern when $\Delta\nu / J$ is large. As the ratio $\Delta\nu / J$ decreases toward unity (forming an AB system), what happens to the appearance of the four-line multiplet?
optionsEn: The two outer lines grow taller and the two inner lines vanish
The four lines collapse into a single broad peak regardless of $J$
The two inner lines grow taller and the two outer lines shrink (roofing effect)
All four lines remain strictly equal in height ($1:1:1:1$)
questions.explanationEn: When $\Delta\nu / J$ decreases into the second-order AB regime (typically $\Delta\nu / J < 10$), quantum-mechanical state mixing causes the intensities of the two inner lines to increase at the expense of the two outer lines—known as the leaning or roofing effect—while the spacing between each outer-inner pair remains equal to $J_{\text{AB}}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct order of aromatic stabilization energy (aromaticity) among the five-membered heterocycles furan, pyrrole, and thiophene is
optionsEn: Furan $>$ Pyrrole $>$ Thiophene
Thiophene $>$ Furan $>$ Pyrrole
Thiophene $>$ Pyrrole $>$ Furan
Pyrrole $>$ Furan $>$ Thiophene
questions.explanationEn: Delocalization of the heteroatom lone pair into the $6\pi$-electron ring decreases as the electronegativity of the heteroatom increases. Because electronegativity increases in the order $\text{S} < \text{N} < \text{O}$, sulfur donates its lone pair most readily (and has favorable ring bond angles), making thiophene the most aromatic, followed by pyrrole, and furan the least aromatic.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The Paal-Knorr synthesis converts a $1,4$-dicarbonyl compound into a substituted pyrrole upon heating with
optionsEn: ammonia or a primary amine ($\text{RNH}_2$)
hydroxylamine hydrochloride followed by $\text{NaOH}$
Lawesson's reagent or $\text{P}_4\text{S}_{10}$
$\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$ alone
questions.explanationEn: In the Paal-Knorr synthesis, a $1,4$-diketone condenses with ammonia or a primary amine ($\text{RNH}_2$) via sequential hemiaminal formation, cyclization, and dehydration to yield a $2,5$-disubstituted pyrrole. Using $\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$ gives a furan, while $\text{P}_4\text{S}_{10}$ or Lawesson's reagent gives a thiophene.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding characteristic infrared (IR) stretching frequencies is(are)
optionsEn: Conjugation of a ketone carbonyl with a $\text{C=C}$ double bond lowers $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ by approximately $25\text{--}40\text{ cm}^{-1}$
Terminal alkynes ($\text{R-C}\equiv\text{C-H}$) display a sharp $\equiv\text{C-H}$ stretch near $3300\text{ cm}^{-1}$
Aldehydes typically exhibit a characteristic Fermi doublet for the aldehydic $\text{C-H}$ stretch near $2720$ and $2820\text{ cm}^{-1}$
A $\gamma$-lactone (5-membered cyclic ester) absorbs at a lower $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ than an acyclic ester
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Conjugation delocalizes $\pi$-electrons and lowers the $\text{C=O}$ bond order, reducing $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ from $\sim 1715$ to $\sim 1680\text{ cm}^{-1}$. (B) True: High $s$-character ($sp$) of the terminal alkyne $\text{C-H}$ gives a sharp band near $3300\text{ cm}^{-1}$. (C) True: Interaction of the aldehydic $\text{C-H}$ stretch with the first overtone of the $\text{C-H}$ bend produces the diagnostic Fermi doublet at $2720/2820\text{ cm}^{-1}$. (D) False: Ring strain in a 5-membered $\gamma$-lactone raises $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ to $\sim 1770\text{ cm}^{-1}$, higher than acyclic esters ($\sim 1735\text{ cm}^{-1}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding the basicity of nitrogen heterocycles in aqueous solution is(are)
optionsEn: Piperidine is a much stronger base than pyridine
Pyridine is a much stronger base than pyrrole
Pyrrole is more basic than pyridine because its lone pair is in an $sp^3$ orbital
Imidazole is more basic than pyridine
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Piperidine ($\text{p}K_{a\text{H}} \approx 11.1$) has an $sp^3$ lone pair, whereas pyridine ($\text{p}K_{a\text{H}} \approx 5.2$) has a more tightly held $sp^2$ lone pair. (B) True & (C) False: Pyrrole's lone pair is part of the $6\pi$ aromatic sextet, so protonation destroys aromaticity ($\text{p}K_{a\text{H}} \approx -3.8$). (D) True: Imidazole ($\text{p}K_{a\text{H}} \approx 7.0$) is more basic than pyridine because protonation at the pyridine-like N-3 generates a symmetric, resonance-stabilized imidazolium cation.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding D-glucose and its derivatives is(are)
optionsEn: In aqueous solution, $\beta$-D-glucopyranose is more abundant than $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose because all five ring substituents occupy equatorial positions in the $^4C_1$ chair conformation
D-Glucose and D-mannose are C-2 epimers and therefore yield the exact same phenylosazone upon reaction with excess phenylhydrazine
Treatment of D-glucose with $\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ oxidizes both C-1 and C-6 to yield D-glucaric acid
Methyl $\alpha$-D-glucopyranoside does not undergo mutarotation in neutral aqueous solution
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: $\beta$-D-glucopyranose ($\sim 64\%$) has all bulky substituents equatorial in $^4C_1$, whereas $\alpha$-D-glucopyranose ($\sim 36\%$) has an axial C-1 $-\text{OH}$. (B) True: Osazone formation destroys chirality at C-2, so C-2 epimers D-glucose and D-mannose give identical osazones. (C) False: Mild bromine water ($\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) selectively oxidizes only the C-1 aldehyde to D-gluconic acid (dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ is needed for D-glucaric acid). (D) True: Methyl $\alpha$-D-glucopyranoside is a full acetal (glycoside) and cannot ring-open in neutral water.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of distinct signals observed in the broadband proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum of $1,3,5$-triethylbenzene is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: $1,3,5$-Triethylbenzene possesses three-fold rotational symmetry ($C_{3}$). Its $12$ carbons group into $4$ chemically distinct sets: (1) the three substituted quaternary aromatic carbons (C1, C3, C5), (2) the three unsubstituted aromatic CH carbons (C2, C4, C6), (3) the three equivalent benzylic $-\text{CH}_2-$ carbons, and (4) the three equivalent $-\text{CH}_3$ carbons. Hence, $4$ signals appear.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Given $\text{p}K_{a1} = 2.34$ ($\alpha\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$) and $\text{p}K_{a2} = 9.69$ ($\alpha\text{-NH}_3^+$) for L-alanine, its isoelectric point ($\text{pI}$) is _____ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: For a neutral amino acid with no ionizable side chain, the isoelectric point is the arithmetic mean of $\text{p}K_{a1}$ and $\text{p}K_{a2}$: $\text{pI} = \frac{2.34 + 9.69}{2} = \frac{12.03}{2} = 6.015 \approx 6.02$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Compare the carbonyl stretching frequencies ($\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$) of the following four compounds: (I) methyl benzoate, (II) phenyl acetate, (III) $\delta$-valerolactone (6-membered lactone), and (IV) $\beta$-propiolactone (4-membered lactone). The compound with the HIGHEST and the compound with the LOWEST $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ are, respectively,
optionsEn: (II) and (III)
(IV) and (I)
(II) and (I)
(IV) and (III)
questions.explanationEn: $\beta$-Propiolactone (IV) suffers severe 4-membered ring angle strain, raising $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ to $\sim 1820\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (highest). Phenyl acetate (II) absorbs near $\sim 1765\text{ cm}^{-1}$ because the phenyl ring competes for the ester oxygen lone pair, reducing $+M$ donation to $\text{C=O}$. $\delta$-Valerolactone (III) absorbs near $\sim 1735\text{ cm}^{-1}$, whereas methyl benzoate (I) has direct aryl conjugation with the carbonyl group, lowering $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ to $\sim 1720\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (lowest). Thus, (IV) and (I).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A compound $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ shows an IR band at $1715\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and only TWO signals in its $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum: a $3\text{H}$ triplet at $\delta\; 1.06\text{ ppm}$ ($J = 7.3\text{ Hz}$) and a $2\text{H}$ quartet at $\delta\; 2.42\text{ ppm}$ ($J = 7.3\text{ Hz}$). Its broadband proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum exhibits how many signals, and what is the compound?
optionsEn: $3$ signals; $2,2$-dimethylpropanal
$4$ signals; $3$-methylbutan-$2$-one
$5$ signals; pentan-$2$-one
$3$ signals; pentan-$3$-one
questions.explanationEn: The IR band at $1715\text{ cm}^{-1}$ indicates a saturated acyclic ketone. Only two $^1\text{H}$ NMR signals—a triplet ($3\text{H}$, or $6\text{H}$ total) and a quartet ($2\text{H}$, or $4\text{H}$ total)—identify two symmetry-equivalent ethyl groups attached to a carbonyl, i.e., pentan-$3$-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$). By symmetry, its $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum shows exactly $3$ signals ($\text{C=O}$, $\text{CH}_2$, and $\text{CH}_3$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compounds will show a prominent McLafferty rearrangement fragment ion at $m/z = 74$ in its EI mass spectrum?
optionsEn: Methyl propanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$)
Methyl pentanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$)
Methyl $2,2$-dimethylpropanoate ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOCH}_3$)
Ethyl butanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$)
questions.explanationEn: Methyl esters bearing a $\gamma$-hydrogen on the acyl chain undergo McLafferty rearrangement to form the characteristic enol radical cation $[\text{CH}_2\text{=C(OH)OCH}_3]^{+\bullet}$ at $m/z = 74$ ($3\times 12 + 6\times 1 + 2\times 16 = 74$). Methyl pentanoate ($M = 116$) has $\gamma$-hydrogens and loses propene ($42\text{ Da}$) to give $m/z = 74$. Methyl propanoate and methyl pivalate lack $\gamma$-hydrogens, while ethyl butanoate gives $m/z = 88$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the **Pomeranz-Fritsch synthesis**, condensation of benzaldehyde with $2,2$-diethoxyethan-$1$-amine (aminoacetaldehyde diethyl acetal) followed by acid-catalyzed cyclization ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) yields
optionsEn: Isoquinoline
$1H$-Indole
Cinnoline
Quinoline
questions.explanationEn: In the Pomeranz-Fritsch synthesis, an aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) condenses with aminoacetaldehyde diethyl acetal to form a benzaliminoacetal ($\text{PhCH=NCH}_2\text{CH(OEt)}_2$). Strong acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) protonates an ethoxy group to generate an oxocarbenium ion, which undergoes electrophilic aromatic cyclization and elimination of ethanol to directly produce **isoquinoline**.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following explanations best accounts for the **anomeric effect** observed in $\alpha$-methyl-D-glucopyranoside (where the axial C-1 methoxy conformer is stabilized relative to steric expectations)?
optionsEn: Resonance conjugation between the ring oxygen and the C-2 hydroxyl group
Intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the axial C-1 methoxy oxygen and the C-3 axial hydrogen
Reduced $1,3$-diaxial steric repulsion of an axial $-\text{OMe}$ compared to an equatorial $-\text{OMe}$

Hyperconjugative $n_{\text{O}} \to \sigma^*_{\text{C1--OMe}}$ delocalization from an antiperiplanar lone pair on the ring oxygen into the antibonding orbital of the axial C1–OMe bond, coupled with dipole-dipole minimization
questions.explanationEn: The anomeric effect has two reinforcing origins: (1) Stereoelectronic hyperconjugation: when the C-1 electronegative substituent ($-\text{OMe}$) is axial, an $sp^3$ lone pair on the endocyclic ring oxygen is strictly antiperiplanar ($180^\circ$) to the $\text{C1--OMe}$ bond, enabling stabilizing $n \to \sigma^*$ donation; (2) Electrostatic: the axial orientation aligns the C1–OMe dipole opposed to the ring-oxygen dipole, reducing dipole-dipole repulsion.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding IR and UV-Vis spectroscopy of organic molecules is(are)
optionsEn: In the IR spectrum of *trans*-$1,2$-dichloroethene, the $\text{C=C}$ stretching vibration is IR-inactive due to the center of inversion
Extending the conjugation of a linear polyene by one additional $\text{C=C}$ double bond shifts $\lambda_{\max}$ to a longer wavelength and increases $\varepsilon_{\max}$
In the Woodward-Fieser rules for enones, an $\alpha$-alkyl substituent adds $+10\text{ nm}$ whereas a $\beta$-alkyl substituent adds $+12\text{ nm}$
A cyclic $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone in a five-membered ring has a higher Woodward-Fieser base value ($215\text{ nm}$) than a six-membered cyclic enone ($202\text{ nm}$)
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: *trans*-$1,2$-Dichloroethene ($C_{2h}$) has an inversion center, so its symmetric $\text{C=C}$ stretch produces zero dipole change (IR-inactive, Raman-active). (B) True: Each additional conjugated double bond narrows the HOMO-LUMO gap (bathochromic shift) and increases transition dipole moment (hyperchromic effect). (C) True: Standard Woodward-Fieser increments for enones are $+10\text{ nm}$ ($\alpha$-alkyl) and $+12\text{ nm}$ ($\beta$-alkyl). (D) False: The values are reversed—a 6-membered or acyclic enone has base $215\text{ nm}$, while a 5-membered cyclopentenone has base $202\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding the chemistry of **quinoline** and **isoquinoline** is(are)
optionsEn: Nitration of quinoline with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ occurs preferentially in the carbocyclic benzene ring at C-5 and C-8
Nucleophilic attack by $\text{NaNH}_2$ (Chichibabin reaction) on quinoline occurs predominantly at C-2
Nucleophilic attack by $\text{NaNH}_2$ (Chichibabin reaction) on isoquinoline occurs predominantly at C-1
Electrophilic nitration of isoquinoline with $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ occurs predominantly at C-1 and C-3
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: In strong acid, quinoline is protonated to the quinolinium ion; the electron-deficient pyridine ring is strongly deactivated, so nitration occurs on the benzene ring at C-5 and C-8. (B) True: $\text{NaNH}_2$ attacks the electrophilic C-2 of quinoline to give $2$-aminoquinoline. (C) True: In isoquinoline, attack at C-1 preserves benzene aromaticity in the Meisenheimer intermediate (unlike C-3 attack), giving $1$-aminoisoquinoline. (D) False: Nitration of isoquinoline occurs on the benzene ring at C-5 (major) and C-8, not at C-1/C-3.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct classification(s) of the following natural products is(are)
optionsEn: Menthol ($\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{20}\text{O}$) is a monocyclic monoterpene alcohol
Camphor ($\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}\text{O}$) is a bicyclic monoterpene ketone
Nicotine contains both a pyridine ring and an $N$-methylpyrrolidine ring
Citral ($\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}\text{O}$) is a bicyclic sesquiterpene aldehyde
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Menthol ($2$-isopropyl-$5$-methylcyclohexan-$1$-ol) is a monocyclic $\text{C}_{10}$ monoterpenoid alcohol. (B) True: Camphor is a bicyclic bornane-type $\text{C}_{10}$ monoterpenoid ketone. (C) True: Nicotine is $3$-($1$-methylpyrrolidin-$2$-yl)pyridine, containing both pyridine and $N$-methylpyrrolidine rings. (D) False: Citral (geranial/neral) is an ACYCLIC $\text{C}_{10}$ monoterpene aldehyde, not a bicyclic sesquiterpene.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Given $\text{p}K_{a1} = 2.18$ ($\alpha\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$), $\text{p}K_{a2} = 8.95$ ($\alpha\text{-NH}_3^+$), and $\text{p}K_{aR} = 10.53$ (side-chain $\varepsilon\text{-NH}_3^+$) for L-lysine, its isoelectric point ($\text{pI}$) is _____ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: For a basic amino acid like L-lysine, the net neutral zwitterionic species predominates between the two highest $\text{p}K_a$ values ($\text{p}K_{a2}$ and $\text{p}K_{aR}$). Therefore, $\text{pI} = \frac{\text{p}K_{a2} + \text{p}K_{aR}}{2} = \frac{8.95 + 10.53}{2} = \frac{19.48}{2} = 9.74$.
